chunks: Abdullah ibn al-Nadr ibn Sam'an al-Tamimi (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Makki narrated that Abul Hassan Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Kharani narrated from Salih ibn Zyad, from Abi Uthman Abd ibn Maymun al-Sakoony, from Abdullah ibn Mo'an al-Azdi, from Imran ibn Suleiman, from Tavoos ibn al-Yaman, who said: 'I heard Ali ibn al-Hussein (peace be upon them) say:'

The signs of a believer are five. I asked: 'And what are they, O son of God's Prophet?' He said: 'Piety in private; charity in times of scarcity; patience at the time of calamity; forbearance at the time of anger; and truthfulness at the time of fear.'
ai.seo_question: What are the five signs of a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, this hadith from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) defines the believer's character through five distinct virtues, emphasizing the consistency of faith in both private solitude and public crisis. It highlights the Shia emphasis on *War'* (piety/conscientiousness) as the foundation of inner integrity, linking emotional resilience and truthfulness directly to spiritual maturity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-4 Abdullah ibn al-Nazr ibn Sam’an al-Tamimy - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abul Qasim Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Maliki quoted Abul Hassan Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Kharani, on the authority of Salih ibn Zyad, on the authority of Abi Uthman Abd ibn Maymun al-Sakoony, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mo’an al-Azodi , on the authority of Imran ibn Suleiman , on the authority of Tavoos ibn al-Yaman, “I heard Ali ibn al-Hussein as-Sajjad (MGB) say, ‘There are five signs for a believer.’ I asked the Imam (MGB), ‘O son of God’s Prophet! What are they?’
The Imam (MGB) replied, ‘Piety in private; charity at times of poverty; perseverance at times of calamity; patience at times of anger; truthfulness at times of fear.’”
